summary.oneLiner: Decorous Investment and Trading Company Limited is a small New Delhi-based investment and trading company whose activities span real estate, commission agency/broking, gems & jewellery, consultancy and trading in bullion and commodities.
summary.business: The company describes itself as carrying out business activities relating to real estate, commission, agents, brokers, gems & jewellery, consultancy and trading/service providers, as per the objects contained in its Memorandum of Association. During the year it states it was engaged in commission, agency and broking work, consultancy, trading/purchase and sale of bullion and commodities, and service provision. The annual report contains no description of any manufactured product, brand, customer or contract.

risks.note: The Directors' Report states flatly that 'Risk Management Policy is Not Applicable to your company.' There is no Risk Management Committee, no ERM description and no 'Risks & Concerns' section anywhere in the MD&A, so risks are neither identified nor mitigated in any disclosed process.

risks.risk: Sub-crore operating scale with no disclosed operating asset
risks.note: The Directors' Report states 'Company has received the total revenue of Rs. 59,88,860.00' for FY26. No plant, office footprint, capacity, customer, contract or order book is disclosed anywhere in the report — the company has no operating base from which earnings can be projected.

The company describes itself as simultaneously in real estate, commission/agency and broking, gems & jewellery, consultancy, and trading/purchase and sale of bullion and commodities, 'as per the Objects as contained in MOA'. Nothing in the report shows which of these actually generated the year's income, so the business has no identifiable franchise and no barrier to entry.

risks.risk: Key-person concentration and rapid churn in the WTD/CFO seat
risks.note: The same individual holds Whole-Time Director and CFO simultaneously, and that combined seat changed hands twice within roughly eight months: Raj Kumar Gupta resigned w.e.f. 29.09.2025; Ashok Kumar was appointed WTD cum CFO w.e.f. 01.10.2025, stepped down from the executive role w.e.f. 29.05.2026; Varsha Jain was appointed Additional Executive Director in a whole-time capacity cum CFO w.e.f. 29.05.2026, still subject to members' approval.

The Directors' Report records that BSE levied a fine of Rs. 3,12,700/- by communication dated 14.12.2023 for non-submission of Related Party Transactions in XBRL mode under Reg. 23(9) for the period ended 30.09.2023. The company contested applicability and filed waiver applications dated 04.05.2024, 16.05.2025 and 11.06.2025, with acceptance by BSE only by e-mail dated 23.02.2026 — a multi-year unresolved compliance dispute. (Read in the Directors' Report 'Waiver Application to BSE Ltd.' paragraph, routed into the sibling governance/capex bundles of this same annual report.)

risks.risk: Structural related-party dependence for its own premises and management
risks.note: The report concedes that the only related-party items it considers non-trivial are 'salary to WTD &CFO and Company Secretary as well as Rent for Regd. Office'. Form AOC-2 shows the registered-office rent is paid to an entity interested through a relative of a Director, so the company's premises and its entire management cost sit with connected parties rather than at arm's length in substance.

risks.risk: Commodity and bullion price exposure without disclosed hedging
risks.note: The company states it is engaged in 'trading/ purchase & sale of bullion & commodities'. No hedging policy, position limit or inventory-risk disclosure appears anywhere in the report, so trading outcomes are directly exposed to bullion and commodity price moves.

risks.risk: Outlook rests on generic sector commentary, not company-specific demand
risks.note: The MD&A's entire opportunity case is Indian real-estate industry statistics — 'Real estate contributes about 5% to India's GDP', a CAGR of 11.2% during FY 2020-30, affordable housing and 100 Smart Cities. None of it is tied to a project, land bank, mandate or client of the company, so the stated outlook carries no evidence that the company can capture any of it.
